title: Off-rank stalk vanishing of pulled-back Koszul Ext
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], let $\mathcal I$ be its kernel ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $C=i^*\mathcal I$ be its tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Use the derived category and derived internal Hom of [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and write $F^q=H^q(R\mathcal Hom_Y(i_*\mathcal O_Z,\mathcal O_Y))$. Suppose near every $z\in Z$ an affine neighbourhood of $i(z)$ cuts out $i$ by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let $r:Z\to\mathbb N$ be locally constant with $r(z)=\operatorname{finrank}_{\mathcal O_{Z,z}}C_z$, where the module stalk is [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. For every $q\in\mathbb Z$ and $z\in Z$ with $q\ne r(z)$, the stalk $(i^*F^q)_z$ is zero.

proof.text: Choose an affine Koszul chart at the point, set A to its section ring and I to the kernel ideal. The closed immersion gives the quotient-spectrum identification. The Koszul quotient augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, and exact associated-module sheafification gives a finite free resolution of the restricted structure-sheaf pushforward. Terms above its length vanish by the exterior-power basis; extend the complex to integer degrees.

Restrict derived internal Hom to the chart and compute it by the bounded finite free Hom model into the structure sheaf in degree zero. On standard affine opens, finite free coordinates identify sheaf Hom with associated module Hom and commute with restriction. Homology commutes with exact associated-module sheafification. Use the common K-injective Hom complex to compare the standard and supplied derived universes.
The Koszul conormal basis and affine conormal frame identify the sequence length m with the finrank of C at the chosen point.

The dual Koszul cohomology vanishes in every integer degree except m, including negative degrees. The rank hypothesis identifies m=r(z), and q differs from that value. Hence F^q is zero on an affine neighbourhood of i(z). Pullback of the zero module sheaf is zero, and its stalk at z is zero. Empty sequence and empty source are included.
